advice.roomRead: Roster 10: Picks 30 and 31 back-to-back with TE:high and no TE; only team that can take Bowers before us.
advice.strategy: Balanced start (Nacua/Barkley) now buying the only separating TE, since RB/WR depth at this tier is flat and refillable at 32 and 49.
advice.firstSeedDeviationReason: Reaching one rank past First Seed's best available (fsGap 1) to secure the only tier-1 TE before four TE-needy teams pick.
advice.strongestAlternativeWhy: Pickens is First Seed's best available (rank 28, fsGap 0) and Juancho's simulation pick, giving us a genuine WR2 next to Nacua.
advice.strongestCounterargument: Pickens survives 78.3% and Bowers/Pickens are both there in 55.7% of runs, with bIfAGone showing Pickens still alive in 86.2% of runs where Bowers is taken - and Bowers' simGap is -12.7 versus Pickens' -12.2, so the simulation sees them as equal.
advice.whyRecommendationStillWins: Equal simGap means the tiebreak is replaceability: if Pickens goes, the WR8 tier still has 16 members (Higgins, McMillan, McConkey, Nabers all 81-97% to survive); if Bowers goes, our TE falls 23+ points to Loveland/Warren with no recovery. Taking the 74.3% player and collecting the 86-93% ones at 32/49 is the better sequence.
advice.expectedNextPickPlan: At 32 take the best of Pickens/Nabers/Higgins if a WR survives, otherwise a tier-9 RB (Javonte Williams 86%, Judkins 98%, Skattebo 93.7%); QB waits until 49+ since Maye/Hurts/Daniels/Burrow are 97-100% to last.
